constraints_details.result: Slp Stanmore Law Practice, 51 - 53 The Broadway, Stanmore, Harrow, HA7 4DJ

description:
Change of use of the first and second floors from
Office (Use Class E(g)(i)) to 4no. flats (1 x 3-bed, 2 x 2-bed and 1 x 1-bed)
(Use Class C3); extension and retention of the existing ground floor to provide
an enlarged flexible commercial unit (Use Class E); single and two-storey rear
extensions; second-floor rear extension; alterations to the roof to form an
enlarged rear dormer; alterations to the roof of the second-floor extension;
rooflights to the front and both side roof slopes; installation of a biodiverse
roof to the proposed single-storey rear extension; cycle and refuse stores; and
associated external alterations
decision_conditions: <p>The biodiverse roof shall be installed in full accordance with the details and specifications contained within the approved documents, including the roof build-up, substrate specification and composition, planting mix, irrigation arrangements and management and maintenance provisions.</p><p>The biodiverse roof shall be fully installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained, managed and maintained in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development.</p>
<p>The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.</p>

<p>No above ground works shall commence until details and samples of all external materials to be used in the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:</p><p>a) Facing brickwork, including bond, mortar colouring and pointing</p><p>b) External render (where applicable) including colour and finish</p><p>c) Roof coverings</p><p>d) Materials, colour and finish of proposed dormer</p><p>e) External rainwater goods</p><p>f) Windows, external doors, and rooflights, including frame material and colour.</p><p>g) Proposed shopfront including glazing, entrance door and framing.</p><p>h) Hard surfacing materials.</p><p>The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.</p>

<p>Prior to commencement of the development, a proportionate Construction Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include details of construction vehicle access and deliveries, loading and unloading, storage of materials, contractor parking, and measures to minimise dust, noise and obstruction of the highway. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan.</p>

<p>No above ground works shall commence until a Sustainability Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Statement shall demonstrate:</p><p>a) How the development has incorporated energy efficiency improvements through the retrofit of the existing building;</p><p>b) How the proposal has followed the energy hierarchy, including measures to reduce energy demand and improve building performance;</p><p>c) That the residential accommodation will achieve a maximum internal water consumption of 105 litres per person per day, and the commercial unit will achieve the relevant BREEAM Wat 01 standard (or equivalent);</p><p>d) The consideration given to on-site renewable energy generation, including photovoltaic panels and heat pumps, and where such measures are not proposed, a justification demonstrating why they are not feasible or appropriate.</p><p>The sustainability measures approved&nbsp;pursuant to this condition shall thereafter be implemented and retained.</p>

<p>Prior to the first occupation of the development, details of integrated biodiversity enhancement features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the type, number and location of integrated bird nesting features and, where practicable, bat roosting features to be incorporated into the development. The approved features shall be installed prior to the first occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.</p>

<p>Prior to the first occupation of the development, details of the measures to be incorporated into the development to minimise opportunities for crime and anti-social behaviour shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall seek to achieve Secured by Design accreditation and, where accreditation is not achieved, the submitted details shall demonstrate the measures undertaken to seek accreditation, the reasons why accreditation has not been achieved and any alternative security measures incorporated into the development. The approved security measures shall be implemented prior to first occupation and thereafter retained</p>

<p>Notwithstanding those details already submitted, prior to first occupation of the development, full details of the proposed cycle parking facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:</p><p>- The design, dimensions and layout of the cycle stores</p><p>- The materials and finishes to be used</p><p>- Details of the means of enclosure and access arrangements</p><p>- Details of the security measures, including access control and the type of cycle stands to be provided.</p><p>- Details demonstrating that the cycle parking will be secure and enclosed.</p><p>The approved cycle parking facilities shall be provided prior to the first occupation of the residential units and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for cycle parking purposes only.</p>

<p>Notwithstanding those details already submitted, prior to the first occupation of the development, a final Refuse Management Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Strategy shall include:</p><p>a) The design, dimensions, materials and enclosure of the refuse and recycling stores;</p><p>b) The number, size and type of bins to be provided for both the residential and commercial uses, including the separation of waste streams;</p><p>c) Details demonstrating sufficient capacity for the proposed residential accommodation and the permitted commercial use;</p><p>d) The management arrangements for the storage and presentation of refuse and recycling for collection, including the collection point, collection method and frequency;</p><p>e) Details of the security and accessibility of the refuse stores.</p><p>The approved refuse storage facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development and thereafter retained and managed in accordance with the approved Refuse Management Strategy.</p>
<p>The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the submitted Fire Safety Statement Form dated 06 January 2026, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p>

<p>The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the recommendations and mitigation measures contained within the approved Noise Impact Assessment (Phlorum Ltd, Ref. 14480A (NV) V1, dated February 2026). The approved glazing, ventilation and any other acoustic mitigation measures identified within the assessment shall be installed prior to the first occupation of the residential units and shall thereafter be permanently retained and maintained.</p>
